This miscellaneous appeal by appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988

is arising out of the Award dated 19.09.2014 passed by Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (hereinafter it would be referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 192/2014 seeking on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.
3.

As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Indrapal Singh, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.7,65,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
4. Counsel for appellants submitted that compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal in assessing the income of deceased to the tune of Rs.4,000/- per month is inadequate and is on the lower side.
It is further submitted that deceased was unskilled labour at the time of alleged accident.

Learned counsel for the claimants contended that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased and in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20417 2 MA-148-2015 not adding any future prospects as well as reasonable other heads i.e. loss of estate,
loss of consortium, funeral expenses etc.

Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of Smt.Chandrakali vs Raju on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109252001/
1 compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

sentences.text: 5 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased is on lower side.

In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased in the present case is Rs.4,945/- per month of an unskilled labour instead of Rs.4,000/- per month which has wrongly been assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

8. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for future prospects of 40%.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, Claims Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 15.
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs.4945/- pm  Future Prospects@40% (Rs.4945+ 1978)= Rs.69  Annual Income Rs.83076/-

After deducting dependency 1/4 Rs.62307/-
 Multiplier (15) Rs.934605/-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 6 = Rs.2,
 Other heads Rs.30000/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20417  3   Total Compensation = Rs.12 10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case i s Rs.12,04,605/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs. 7,65,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.4,39,605/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,39,605/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
13. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
